newsitem.title: USA: IPO HIGHLIGHTS - Wall St cheers Rambus.
newsitem.headline: IPO HIGHLIGHTS - Wall St cheers Rambus.

text.p: Shares of Rambus Inc soared at their debut on Wednesday, gaining 16-3/8 or 136.5 percent to reach 28-3/8 in afternoon trading. Over 4.7 million shares had traded hands.

A warm reception had been indicated when the price range for the 2.75 million share issue, lead-managed by Morgan Stanley, was earlier raised to $10 to $12 a share from $8 to $10. The deal priced at $12 per share.

Mountain View, Calif.-based Rambus has developed an interface technology which allows data to be transferred between most semiconductor chips at considerably greater speeds than is permitted by conventional systems. It has licensed its technology to a host of leading dynamic random access memory (DRAMs) chip makers.
Mark Basham, investment officer at Standard & Poor's, said that the company's "very promising technology" and "agreements with key semiconductor firms like Intel Corp " made its IPO a hot investment.
Rambus has a pact with Intel to develop a version of its technology for use in Intel chips.
Basham said the success of this deal will make it a little easier for underwriters to take technology companies public over the summer. "The floodgates have opened a little bit," he said.
Ocwen Asset Investment Corp's deal also received a welcome, albeit less spectacular, from investors. Shares were up 2-1/2 to 18-1/2, on heavy trading of 8.9 million shares.

The real estate investment trust's (REIT) 15 million shares were priced at $16 each in a deal led by Friedman, Billings, Ramsey & Co. The company had originally filed for a 12.5 million share offering.
The company's primary focus will be investments in distressed properties. According to its filing, it will be managed by Ocwen Capital Corp, a wholly-owned subsidiary of Ocwen Financial Corp.
After the offering, Ocwen Financial will own about 13 percent of the REIT's common stock, assuming that the underwriters do not exercise their over-allotment option.
Hawaiian Natural Water Co Inc also made its debut on Wednesday with two million units priced at $4 each. The units rose to $5 by the afternoon.
Each unit equals one common share and one warrant. Joseph Stevens was lead underwriter on the deal.
The company bottles, markets, and distributes water.
